If you have ever tried setting up VoIP calls over the internet, you have probably run into the NAT wall.
Packets go out and somehow don’t come back. SIP signaling breaks, RTP streams vanish, and you’re left staring at dead air. entry.title: Understanding High Availability day 44 of system design basics
entry.summary:
In this post, we'll explore the concept of availability, break down availability tiers, and discuss strategies and best practices for achieving high availability in system design. What is Availability? Availability measures the proportion of time a system is operational and accessible when needed. It's typically expressed as a percentage, representing the system's uptime over a specific period. The formal definition is: Availability = Uptime / (Uptime + Downtime) Uptime: The time a system is functional and accessible. Downtime: The time a system is unavailable due to failures, maintenance, or other issues.
For example, a system with 99.9% availability is down for less than 9 hours per year, while 99.99% availability reduces downtime to under 1 hour per year. Availability Tiers Availabi…
